pages.title: Overview
pages.summary: What Oncall keeps, how it sits beside your pager, and where to start.

pages.title: Install and run
pages.summary: Run locally or deploy to your Cloudflare account, sign in by email, and remove your hosted installation.

pages.title: Team and sign-in
pages.summary: How people sign in, what admins, responders and viewers can do, and how to add someone.

pages.title: Schedules and hand-overs
pages.summary: Set primary and backup rotations, hand-overs across clock changes, swaps and your calendar feed.

pages.title: Incidents and alerts
pages.summary: Declare and work an incident, keep its timeline and follow-ups, and route alerts.

pages.title: Changes and dependencies
pages.summary: Connect authenticated change senders and inspect recent changes beside services, alerts and incidents.

pages.title: Reports and reviews
pages.summary: Understand response timings, inspect retained review material and accept evidenced improvements.

pages.title: Move in from Opsgenie or PagerDuty
pages.summary: Bring your rota across from saved export files, review it, then apply or undo it.

pages.title: Compatible alert intake
pages.summary: Connect existing PagerDuty, Opsgenie and Splunk-shaped senders with explicit lifecycle receipts and paging OFF.

pages.title: Routed intake keys
pages.summary: Route compatible monitoring events to allowed services with versioned rules, replay and an unrouted queue.

pages.title: Export and restore
pages.summary: Take everything with you, restore it into a new installation, or start over.

pages.title: What Oncall does not do
pages.summary: Paging, decisions and outside accounts Oncall leaves alone, stated plainly.

pages.title: Command reference
pages.summary: Local and hosted commands, their flags and what they change.
